items.prompt: Which material is transparent?

options.why: Wood is opaque. Light cannot pass through it.
Metal is opaque. You cannot see through it.
Cardboard is opaque. It blocks light.

hints: Transparent means you can see through it.
Think about what windows are made of.
Which material lets light pass straight through?
items.explanation: Clear glass is transparent, so light passes through it and you can see through it. That is why windows are made of glass.

items.prompt: Match each object to the property that makes its material useful.
hints: Think about the job each object does.
A towel's job is to dry you.
Start with the window. What must you be able to do through it?
items.explanation: A window must let light through, an umbrella must keep rain out and a towel must soak up water. A rubber band must stretch and a hammer head must be hard and strong.

items.prompt: Sort these materials. Are they waterproof?
hints: Waterproof materials do not let water through.
Think about what happens to each material in the rain.
Start with paper. Does it keep water out?
items.explanation: Plastic, rubber, glass and metal do not let water through, so they are waterproof. Paper, cotton, cardboard and sponge let water in or soak it up.

items.prompt: A spoon can be made of metal, wood or plastic. What is metal?

options.why: An object is a thing, like a spoon. Metal is what it is made from.
A property describes a material, like hard or shiny.

hints: An object is a thing you can pick up and use.
Ask: is metal the thing, or what the thing is made of?
What do we call the stuff an object is made from?
items.explanation: Metal is a material, the stuff an object is made from. The spoon is the object.

items.prompt: Rubber is used to make boots for rainy days. Which two properties make it a good choice?

options.why: Boots do not need to be see-through. They need to keep water out.
Absorbent boots would soak up water, and your feet would get wet.
These properties do not help keep feet dry.

hints: Think about the job of a rain boot.
It must keep water out and let your feet move.
Which pair of words matches both jobs?
items.explanation: Rubber is waterproof, so it keeps feet dry. It is also flexible, so the boot bends as you walk.

items.prompt: Choose 2 properties a good raincoat material needs.

options.why: An absorbent coat would soak up rain and get heavy.
A rigid coat would not bend when you move your arms.
A raincoat must not break or tear easily.

hints: A raincoat must keep you dry.
It must also let you move freely.
Find one word about water and one about bending.
items.explanation: A raincoat must be waterproof to keep rain out. It must also be flexible so you can move.

items.prompt: Which material is best for a frying pan?

options.why: Plastic can melt on a hot stove.
Wood could burn on a hot stove.
Ordinary glass can crack if it is heated quickly.

hints: A frying pan sits on a very hot stove.
Think about which materials melt, burn or crack in heat.
Which material are most pans in your kitchen made of?
items.explanation: Metal does not melt, burn or crack on a stove, and it is strong. Heat also passes through metal well to cook the food.

items.prompt: A ruler must stay straight when you draw lines. Which property does its material need?

options.why: A stretchy ruler would bend and give wobbly lines.
Soaking up water does not help a ruler draw straight lines.
A soft ruler would bend or dent.

hints: Think about what happens if a ruler bends.
The word means stiff and hard to bend.
Which word is the opposite of flexible?
items.explanation: A ruler must be rigid, which means stiff. A rigid ruler does not bend, so the lines stay straight.

items.prompt: Ana tests how much water four fabrics soak up. Which fabric is best for a towel?

head: Fabric
Water soaked up (ml)
figure.alt: Table of water soaked up: fabric A 5 ml, fabric B 25 ml, fabric C 12 ml, fabric D 0 ml.

options.why: Fabric A soaked up only 5 ml.
Fabric C soaked up 12 ml, less than one other fabric.
Fabric D soaked up nothing. It might make a good raincoat instead.

hints: A towel needs to soak up water.
Find the biggest number in the table.
Compare the numbers in the water column.
items.explanation: A towel should be very absorbent. Fabric B soaked up the most water, 25 ml, so it is the best choice.

items.prompt: Why is paper a poor material for a cup?

options.why: Paper is very light. Weight is not the problem.

options.text: Paper soaks up water and goes soft.

options.why: Most paper is opaque. That is not the problem.

hints: Think about what a cup holds.
What happens to paper when it gets wet?
Look for the property that matters for holding drinks.
items.explanation: Paper is absorbent, so it soaks up drinks and goes soft. Paper cups have a thin waterproof coating to stop this.

items.prompt: A material is hard, shiny and opaque. It rings when tapped. It bends a little without breaking. What is it most likely to be?

options.why: Glass is usually transparent, and it breaks instead of bending.
Wood is not shiny like this and does not ring when tapped.
Rubber is soft and bendy, not hard and shiny.

hints: Check each clue one at a time.
Which materials are shiny and ring like a bell?
Cross out any material that does not match a clue.
items.explanation: Metals are hard, shiny and opaque, and many ring when tapped. Thin metal can bend without breaking.

items.prompt: Choose a material for a school lunch box. Give two reasons, using property words.

criteria.label: Gives two properties, such as waterproof or strong
Links each property to the job of a lunch box

items.model: I would choose plastic. It is waterproof, so juice will not leak out. It is also strong and light, so it will not break in my bag.
hints: Think about what a lunch box must do every day.
Use words like waterproof, strong, light or easy to clean.
items.explanation: Plastic or metal are good choices. They are waterproof and strong, so the food stays clean and the box lasts.

items.prompt: Which word means you can see through a material?

options.why: Opaque means light cannot go through.
Absorbent means it soaks up liquid.

hints: It is the opposite of opaque.
items.explanation: A transparent material lets light go through. We can see clearly through it.

items.prompt: Which material is rigid?
items.explanation: A steel ruler does not bend easily, so it is rigid.

items.prompt: What does absorbent mean?
hints: It is the opposite of waterproof.
items.explanation: An absorbent material, like a sponge, soaks up liquid.

items.prompt: Why are electric cables covered in plastic?

options.text: Plastic does not let electricity pass through.
Plastic soaks up water like a sponge.

items.explanation: Plastic is an insulator. It keeps the electricity inside the wire and keeps us safe.

items.prompt: Which property makes foil good for wrapping food?
items.explanation: Foil is thin and flexible, so it wraps around food easily.

items.prompt: A material is soft, stretchy and waterproof. Which object could it make?

options.why: Windows must be rigid and clear.
Pans must be hard and heat-proof.

items.explanation: A swimming cap must stretch to fit and keep the hair dry.

items.prompt: A cycle helmet is hard outside and soft inside. Why?

options.text: The soft inside is for decoration.
The hard outside is for keeping warm.
The hard outside protects. The soft inside cushions.
The helmet is made of one material.

items.explanation: The hard shell stops sharp objects. The soft lining cushions the head.

items.prompt: Mei scratches four materials with a coin. A scratches easily. B does not. What is she testing?
items.explanation: A hard material is difficult to scratch. Mei is testing hardness.

items.prompt: How can you test whether a fabric is waterproof?

options.text: Drop water on it and see if it soaks in.
Bend it and see if it folds.
Hold it up to the light.

items.explanation: If water beads up or runs off, the fabric is waterproof. If it soaks in, it is not.

items.prompt: Is the material flexible or rigid? Sort the cards.
items.explanation: A rubber band, wool and paper bend easily. Glass, a brick and a steel ruler do not.

items.prompt: How much light goes through? Sort the materials.
items.explanation: Clear glass and clear plastic let all light through. Tracing paper and frosted glass let some through. Wood and metal block it.

items.prompt: Choose all the properties most metals have.
hints: You cannot see through a spoon.
items.explanation: Most metals are hard, shiny and strong. They are not soft and fluffy or see-through.

items.prompt: Choose all the waterproof materials.
items.explanation: Plastic, rubber and glass keep water out. Cotton and sponges soak water up.

items.prompt: Match each property to an object that uses it.
items.explanation: A kitchen towel soaks up spills. Rain boots keep water out. A window lets light through and a rubber band bends and stretches.

items.prompt: Order the materials from the hardest to the softest.
hints: A sponge is softer than wood.
items.explanation: A steel nail is the hardest. A wooden block is hard, a sponge is soft and cotton wool is the softest.

items.prompt: A ___ material lets light through. An ___ material soaks up water.
items.explanation: A transparent material lets light through. An absorbent material soaks up water.

items.prompt: Each fabric had 50 ml of water poured on it. How much is left?
head: Fabric
Soaked (ml)
Left (ml)
items.explanation: The water left is 50 minus the water soaked up. Cotton leaves 10 ml, wool leaves 25 ml and nylon leaves 45 ml.

items.prompt: Ana tests four materials for a bag: leather, nylon, paper and tissue. Leather and nylon do not tear. Paper tears when it is wet. Tissue falls apart. Nylon is the lightest.

parts.prompt: Which material is strong and the lightest?
Which material tears when it is wet?

hints: Strong means it does not tear.
items.explanation: Nylon does not tear and is the lightest. Paper tears when it is wet.

items.prompt: Ravi tests 8 materials. 5 are waterproof. How many are not waterproof?
items.explanation: 8 - 5 = 3 materials are not waterproof.

items.prompt: Tap the transparent object.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: glass, brick, paper and wooden spoon.

items.explanation: Glass is transparent. We can see through it.

items.prompt: Tap the two flexible things.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: rubber band, fabric, brick and rock.

items.explanation: A rubber band and fabric bend easily. A brick and a rock are rigid.

items.prompt: A material that soaks up water is ___.
hints: It is the opposite of waterproof.
items.explanation: An absorbent material soaks up liquid, like a sponge or towel.

items.prompt: Tom needs a lid that is waterproof, strong and light. Material A is waterproof, strong and heavy. B is waterproof, strong and light. C is light, weak and soaks up water. Which is best?

options.why: It is weak and absorbs water.

items.explanation: Material B has all three properties Tom needs.

items.prompt: A material is transparent and flexible. Which object is it likely to make?

options.why: A rubber ball is not transparent.

hints: It must be clear and bendy.
items.explanation: Clear plastic wrap lets light through and bends easily.

items.prompt: Four fabrics soak up 10, 30, 5 and 25 ml of water. Which is best for a towel?

options.text: the one that soaks up 5 ml
the one that soaks up 10 ml
the one that soaks up 30 ml

hints: It should soak up a lot.
items.explanation: A towel should soak up as much water as possible. 30 ml is the most.
